body.statement: For rational input of total encoding length \(B\), compatibility and the endpoints are evaluable in \(O(mr+k\log k)\) arithmetic and comparison operations using \(c_{(\cdot)}\). Endpoint-attaining laws with support at most \(N_\star\), atom denominators dividing \(D\) for the lower endpoint and dividing \(D(\ell-1)\) for an upper endpoint certified by an active subset of size \(\ell\), and active-affine or minimum-cut optimality certificates are constructible and checkable in time polynomial in \(m,r,k,B\). Zero cells cause no division.
body.justification: Sparse exact primal laws and short dual cuts turn a sharpness theorem into an auditable computational result.
body.gap: Generic response-signature linear programs are sharp but can be exponentially represented and do not supply this structured endpoint evaluator or certificate size bound.
body.consumer: A regulator or replication archive can verify every supplied categorical margin and endpoint using exact arithmetic without trusting a black-box exponential linear program.
body.proof_tex:
Compatibility is checked by the \(mr\) inequalities \(e_{is}\geq o_{is}\) together with the supplied simplex checks.  All reduced coordinates require \(O(mr)\) additions.  The lower endpoint is evaluated from \(H\) and the \(k\) values \(b_i-H+h_i\) in \(O(k)\) further operations.  For the upper endpoint, if \(c_{(1)}\leq\cdots\leq c_{(k)}\), then for every \(2\leq\ell\leq k\),
\[
 \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal J,\ |S|=\ell}\sum_{j\in S}c_j
 =\sum_{u=1}^{\ell}c_{(u)}.
\]
Sorting once and scanning prefix sums therefore evaluates every subset-cardinality candidate in \(O(k\log k)\) operations.  This proves the advertised \(O(mr+k\log k)\) arithmetic-and-comparison bound.

We next audit support.  Start from at most \(m\) positive factual cells.  Splitting queried factual blocks into \(B_i,D_i\) adds at most \(k\) cells.  In the upper construction, selecting the \(k\) pieces \(K_i\), the one piece \(K_0\), and the \(k\) residual successes adds at most \(2k+1\) cells by the \(\operatorname{TAKE}\) lemma.  Thus its indicator law has at most \(m+3k+1\) cells.  In the lower construction there are exactly \(k^2\) possible middle edges, because each of the \(k\) left vertices has the edge to block \(0\) and \(k-1\) non-diagonal queried-block edges.  Realizing all positive edge flows adds at most \(k^2\) cells, and residual filling adds at most \(k\), so the lower indicator law has at most \(m+k^2+2k\) cells.

For each categorical coordinate, allocating the first \(r-1\) labels in each of its inside- and outside-factual-stratum domains adds at most \(2(r-1)\) cells; the last label receives the remainder.  Over all \(m\) coordinates this adds at most \(2m(r-1)\).  Consequently each endpoint construction has support at most
\[
 \max\{m+3k+1,m+k^2+2k\}+2m(r-1)
 \leq m+2m(r-1)+k^2+3k+1=N_\star.
\]
Zero domains invoke the no-split branch of \(\operatorname{TAKE}\), so the count remains valid on every boundary face.

Suppose now that the input is rational and let \(D\) be the least common multiple of all input denominators.  Then all input masses and all reduced coordinates are in \(D^{-1}\mathbb Z\), and \(\log_2D\) is at most the sum of the input denominator bit lengths, hence at most \(B\).  For the lower network, scale capacities by \(D\).  Starting from zero, augmenting by the smallest residual capacity on a path keeps every flow integral; after scaling back, all flow pieces and every later \(\operatorname{TAKE}\) split lie in \(D^{-1}\mathbb Z\).

A polynomial exact implementation is obtained by choosing a shortest residual augmenting path at every step.  Residual shortest-path distances never decrease.  If an oriented edge is a bottleneck, later becomes available again through cancellation, and is a bottleneck again, the distance to its tail has increased by at least two.  Thus each oriented edge is a bottleneck at most the number of vertices, there are \(O(k^2)\) edges and \(O(k)\) vertices, and there are \(O(k^3)\) augmentations; each breadth-first search and update costs \(O(k^2)\) arithmetic operations.  All scaled flows are bounded by \(D\), while a middle capacity is \(2D\), so their bit lengths are \(O(B)\).  This gives, conservatively, \(O(k^5)\) exact operations with polynomial bit cost.

For the upper endpoint, if an active certificate is \(g\) or a marginal \(a_j\), then \(t\in D^{-1}\mathbb Z\).  If an active subset has size \(\ell\), then
\[
 t=\frac{\sum_{j\in S}c_j}{\ell-1}
 \in\frac{1}{D(\ell-1)}\mathbb Z.
\]
The initialization \((t-c_i)_+\), sequential enlargement within capacities, residual demands, and categorical demands use only addition, subtraction, minimum, and comparison, so the grid-preservation part of the \(\operatorname{TAKE}\) lemma shows that every final upper atom has denominator dividing \(D(\ell-1)\).  No step divides by a cell mass.

The endpoint constructions perform only polynomially many selections on lists of at most \(N_\star\) cells.  A final atom records one rational weight, one factual treatment, and \(m\) outcome labels, so its encoding length is polynomial in \(m,r,k,B\).  Exact checking sums atom weights for every observational and intervention cell and evaluates the conjunction, also in polynomial time.  For an upper certificate, list an attaining piece among \(g\), a marginal, or a subset \(S\); its valid affine inequality was proved in the upper lemma.  For a lower certificate, list the attaining cut among the empty-left cut, the all-left cut, or a singleton-left cut; the cut enumeration proves its value.  Equality between that dual value and the supplied primal law proves optimality.  Ties permit any attaining certificate.  This establishes construction, verification, denominator, support, and bit-complexity claims.
